transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Samir Rao (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE); Olivia Sanchez (MeridianPay - Head of InfoSec), Daniel Park (MeridianPay - Platform Eng), Ravi Menon (MeridianPay - CTO)

Summary: short demo of data retention controls in Console + API, answered questions on PII redaction, request storage toggles, and KMS.

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we said 30 minutes but we'll run about 40. Quick intros?
00:18 - Olivia: Olivia here, Head of InfoSec at MeridianPay, main focus is data residency and retention.
00:28 - Ravi: Ravi, CTO, interested in operational cost and latency.
00:35 - Daniel P: Daniel, platform eng, will help run POC.
00:43 - Maya: Great. Samir will run the demo. We're going to show Console toggles, API flags, and talk through KMS and SOC2.
01:05 - Samir: Ok jumping into the Console, if you look under Project -> Data Controls, you can see request storage is on/off. By default hosted api stores requests for 30 days for debugging. You can flip storage off per route or globally.
01:40 - Daniel P: So when storage is off, is anything written to logs? What's retained for debugging?
01:55 - Samir: Good question. When storage is off there's minimal telemetry - we keep request metadata for SLOs (timestamp, latency, error codes) but not the prompt/inputs. There is also an optional redaction layer that strips PII before any storage.
02:20 - Olivia: When you say PII redaction, how deterministic is it? We need guarantees for card numbers, SSNs and email addresses.
02:40 - Samir: Our redaction engine uses regex and an ML model to detect entities; we provide a configurable policy where you can set strictness levels. The strict mode will remove card number patterns and common SSNs; we also support custom regex rules you upload. There is a small false negative rate so for PCI you'd typically pair it with client-side tokenization.
03:10 - Ravi: Client-side tokenization - we prefer that for payment PANs. Is that supported?
03:20 - Samir: Yep. You can absolutely tokenize sensitive fields before calling the API; Redwood supports detokenization hooks in Private deployments if needed.
03:40 - Maya: Quick note, for compliance customers often keep storage off and use audit logs plus request-replay on a per-incident basis.
04:05 - Daniel K: jumping in, in the API you can override per request: header x-redwood-store: false. That toggles storage for just that call. Works well for PCI scoped routes.
04:30 - Daniel P: If we toggle off mid-flow, what happens to streaming responses and kv cache? Any impact to latency?
04:50 - Samir: Streaming unaffected; KV cache is orthogonal - cache operations still happen in-memory for the session but we don't persist input to disk if storage is disabled. Latency impact is minimal, redaction step adds ~5-12ms depending on payload size in strict mode.
05:10 - Olivia: Is the redaction executed before logs leave our region? We're concerned about data egress and residency.
05:30 - Samir: Yes, for hosted regions the redact step runs in-region. For Private deployments you manage network, and for Dedicated we can pin serving to a region.
05:50 - Ravi: Can you point to the KMS/HSM flow? We need to ensure keys are customer-owned for sensitive data.
06:05 - Samir: In Private mode you can bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) via KMS/HSM; in Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS integrations so you can rotate keys and we never have plaintext. For hosted we have a managed KMS but can do a partner HSM integration on enterprise contracts.
06:35 - Olivia: Do you log keys or key IDs anywhere?
06:45 - Samir: We store KMS key IDs for routing; we don't log key material. Key IDs are audited in our control-plane logs which are accessible via the Console or exported to your SIEM.
07:05 - Daniel P: About audit logs - retention configurable? We need 7 years for some artifacts.
07:15 - Maya: Audit logs retention is a separate product add-on - default 90 days, can extend to multi-year with enterprise package. We'll share SLAs.
07:35 - Olivia: Can you demonstrate redaction live?
07:45 - Samir: Sure. I'm going to paste a sample payload with a fake card number: 4111 1111 1111 1111 and an email olivia@meridianpay.com, and toggle x-redwood-store: true so you can see the before/after.
08:10 - [typing sounds]
08:25 - Samir: Sending... transcript shows in the console request inspector. You can see the stored request now - card number redacted to [REDACTED_CARD], email to [REDACTED_EMAIL]. Note transcription noise: sometimes the console shows speaker name as "Speaker 1" if we can't map.
08:45 - Olivia: Ok that's promising. What about search in stored requests - does redaction affect searchability?
09:00 - Samir: We index only the redaction-safe tokens; for example we keep hash placeholders so you can search by hashed identifier, but raw card numbers are never indexed.
09:20 - Ravi: Can we get deterministic hashing to join logs with our internal records?
09:30 - Samir: Yes, we support salted deterministic hashing where the salt can be customer-provided in Private deployments. For hosted there's a managed-salt option.
09:45 - Daniel P: You mentioned per-route toggles earlier. Can we set default deny for storage and opt-in per route?
10:00 - Samir: Absolutely. The Console supports a default policy and route overrides. You can also enforce via a policy-as-code pipeline using our API.
10:20 - Olivia: What about retention on embeddings & vector store? We stage embeddings for feature store?
10:35 - Samir: The embeddings API has similar retention toggles. We can choose not to persist embeddings or to store them in a customer VPC. If you need no storage, you can use ephemeral mode where embeddings are returned only in the response and never persisted.
11:00 - Maya: Some customers worry that logging for debugging leaks token-level content during streaming. We have a streaming redact pipeline that applies the same entity rules to each chunk. There is a small lag as it buffers but typical is <20ms.
11:25 - Ravi: How do you validate redaction accuracy? Do you have SOC2 controls around it?
11:35 - Samir: We test redaction with a suite of synthetic datasets and 3rd-party audits. SOC2 covers the control environment, and we also publish redaction test coverage for enterprise customers. We'll include the report.
11:55 - Olivia: Fine, we want to see that report. Also need clarity on what happens in an edge-case where redaction fails - are you able to purge stored artifacts?
12:15 - Samir: Yes, we have a purge API. You can request immediate purge of an object; for hosted we also have an emergency purge escalation with SLA. Purges are logged in the audit trail.
12:35 - Daniel P: How does this tie into model rollouts? If a canary model behaves differently with PII detection, can we auto-fallback?
12:50 - Samir: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates with rollouts: you can set policy to A/B or canary and auto-fallback to a safe variant if evals show regressions on redaction or hallucination metrics.
13:10 - Maya: Let's show the API quick. In the SDK you can set request metadata and the header x-redwood-store: false; also a redaction_level param = strict|normal|off.
13:35 - [Samir types code]
13:50 - Samir: Example response: {"id":"req_123","stored":false,"redaction_applied":"strict"} - note we often show simplified fields in SDK responses. Sorry if the mock console truncates brackets, transcription isn't perfect.
14:10 - Ravi: Curious about cost implication. Does strict redaction or additional audit logging increase cost?
14:25 - Samir: There's a small compute overhead for strict redaction - typically 1-3% of token cost on hosted. Audit log retention beyond default has storage charges. For Dedicated/Private you control infrastructure cost. Redwood Optimize can help suggest tradeoffs.
14:50 - Olivia: For procurement we need pricing for hosted with storage off and for Dedicated with BYOK.
15:00 - Maya: We'll send a pricing sheet; we'll show both per-token hosted and committed capacity for Dedicated.
15:10 - Daniel P: Another question: Do you support SSO with SCIM and RBAC for separating access to stored data?
15:20 - Samir: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and fine-grained RBAC. You can restrict who can view stored requests and who can run purge.
15:35 - Olivia: Can RBAC be synced with AD groups?
15:40 - Samir: Yep, group mapping via SCIM.
15:45 - Daniel K: Quick demo of the audit log view - shows a table with actions, actor, resource, timestamp. You can export as JSON or stream to your SIEM via webhook or S3.
16:10 - Daniel P: If we stream to our SIEM, do you ever send raw prompts?
16:20 - Samir: No, by default the SIEM integration streams audit trail metadata only; you can optionally stream full objects but that's disabled by default and requires explicit consent.
16:35 - Olivia: Ok good. For PCI we likely want storage off and client-side tokenization, but we still want to run debug traces occasionally - what's the recommended workflow?
16:50 - Samir: Common approach: storage off globally, use per-request storage flags to enable ephemeral storage for debug with automatic TTL of 24 hours, and use deterministic hashing to correlate logs. All debug artifacts should be purged automatically.
17:10 - Ravi: If we do a POC, what's the typical timeline and success criteria?
17:20 - Maya: Typical POC 4-6 weeks: week 1 onboarding and sample payload ingestion, week 2 integration and redaction tuning, week 3 latency/throughput benchmark, week 4 wrap-up and decision. Success criteria usually: redaction FNR below threshold, latency within 10% of baseline, and verify purge and audit controls.
17:45 - Olivia: We'll need the onboarding checklist.
17:50 - Maya: We'll share a checklist and a sample benchmark script.
18:00 - Daniel P: About benchmarking - can you run on our sample workload against Dedicated nodes?
18:10 - Samir: We can run a benchmark on Redwood Dedicated in a trial capacity or run a hosted-simulated benchmark. For realistic numbers Dedicated is recommended.
18:30 - Ravi: Any known caveats with KV cache + redaction? Could cache leak PII?
18:40 - Samir: The KV cache is in-memory and ephemeral for the session. If you use storage off, nothing persists; however long-lived caches in Dedicated could be configured to flush. We'll document recommended flush policies.
19:05 - Olivia: On legal side we need data processing addendum and DPA.
19:12 - Maya: We'll attach DPA and standard DP terms in the follow-up email.
19:20 - Olivia: Also need ISO certs?
19:25 - Maya: We have SOC2 Type II; ISO 27001 is on roadmap - we can discuss timelines.
19:40 - Daniel P: A small nit - sometimes the console name for the toggle shows 'store requests' and we've seen customers mis-click it. Any guardrails?
19:55 - Samir: There's an enforced policy mode where only admins can change default storage and you'd need 2FA for changes. We can also add a confirmation modal and audit entry.
20:15 - Olivia: Ok sounds good. Any SLA for purge requests?
20:25 - Samir: Emergency purge SLA is 4 hours for enterprise. Normal purge is 24 hours.
20:35 - Ravi: How do you handle legal holds? If a subpoena arrives, can we put a legal hold on objects?
20:50 - Samir: Yes, we support legal-hold flags that prevent purge for specified objects and log who set the hold. Those holds are manageable via API and Console.
21:10 - Maya: Wrapping up - we'll share security artifacts, pricing for hosted vs dedicated, POC scope and benchmark plan. Any last questions?
21:25 - Olivia: No further questions, please include redaction test coverage in the pack.
21:35 - Ravi: Add margin estimates for cost with strict redaction.
21:40 - Maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
21:45 - [call ends]

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-attributed speaker labels and small transcription errors (e.g., "store requests" shown as "stored requests").
